The Re-rental Program

Affordable apartments in TFC buildings across New York City.

TF Cornerstone offers apartments through New York City’s Re-Rental Program — homes with rent capped by New York City Rent Guidelines Board & Monitoring Agencies, available to income-qualified renters across many of our Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Long Island City buildings.

How This Works in NYC

A portion of apartments in New York City are designated as affordable units under a regulatory agreement with the City. Rent for these apartments is capped and set by the New York City Rent Guidelines Board & Monitoring Agencies, not by landlords. When one becomes available again, it’s offered to income-qualified renters through a process called a re-rental.

Every re-rental was originally leased through New York City’s affordable housing lottery. When the original renter moves out, the apartment doesn’t go back on the open market, it re-rents to another income-qualified household under the same rules. Same building. Same protections. No lottery this time around.

Affordable doesn’t just mean low-income. Many units are set aside for middle- and upper-middle-income households, often people already renting at market rate today.

Who Qualifies

TFC’s affordable units serve a wide range of incomes, from 40% to 165% of Area Median Income (AMI), depending on the building and unit. Each vacancy has its own income guidelines and household size limits.

Many middle-income renters (~120-165% AMI) qualify without realizing it.

Why Many Renters Overlook This

Renters often assume this doesn’t apply to them. Some say:

  • “I probably make too much to qualify”
  • “Affordable housing isn’t for me”
  • “I’ll just deal with the rent increase at renewal”

If any of these sound familiar, it’s worth checking for yourself. Middle- and upper-middle-income earners qualify for a meaningful share of TFC’s affordable inventory.

A Few Things to Know

  • These are called affordable units — not typical market-rate apartments
  • Rent increases are set by City guidelines, not the landlord
  • A unit becomes available when someone moves out
  • Each vacancy has its own income guidelines
  • Income limits vary by unit and household size
  • All income sources are considered
  • Right to lease renewal
  • No broker fees, no application fees

5241 Center Blvd

Building Information

Perched atop the East River waterfront in Hunter's Point South, this Long Island City high-rise offers 1- and 2-bedroom apartments with panoramic views of Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Long Island City steps from the water and steps from the city.

The apartments at 5241 are built for how people actually live. Floor-to-ceiling windows frame the Manhattan skyline from nearly every angle, and select units include private terraces that put those views front and center. Inside, open kitchens, walk-in closets, and in-unit washer/dryers bring the kind of everyday ease that a waterfront Long Island City apartment should deliver.

Amenities at 5241 include a fitness center, yoga room, landscaped rooftop deck, club room, and resident lounge. And because 5241 and 5203 Center Blvd share a connected amenity program, renters get access to an expanded suite next door including a children's playroom, HomeWork co-working space, and additional outdoor common areas. It's two buildings worth of amenities at one address.

Outside, Hunters Point South Park stretches along the waterfront with sweeping skyline views, a kayak ramp, sculpture garden, and one of the most striking urban green spaces in New York City. The Hunters Point South Ferry landing is right across Center Blvd Midtown Manhattan is a short ride across the river, no subway required. The free TFC shuttle to the Vernon-Jackson 7 train adds another easy connection to the rest of the city.

For current availability, visit our on-site leasing office at 5203 Center Blvd in Long Island City.

505 W 37th St

Building Information

505 W 37th St offers over 18,000 square feet of outdoor amenity space and a Sky Club lounge on a high floor with soaring city views. Studio, 1-, 2-, and 3-bedroom apartments feature energy-efficient floor-to-ceiling windows, open layouts, and modern stainless steel appliances with many units including high ceilings, walk-in closets, private balconies, and kitchen windows.

The Sky Club offers billiards, a movie screening setup, and quiet workspaces alongside the views. A second lounge features a grand piano and multiple seating alcoves. HomeWork co-working space is available for dedicated workspace close to home, and the skylit fitness center rounds out the building's indoor amenities.

Penn Station, Port Authority, the High Line, and the Hudson River waterfront are all steps away. Chelsea Piers is walkable along the river.

595 Dean St

Building Information

Rooted in Prospect Heights and steps from Prospect Park, 595 Dean St brings together the best of Brooklyn living brownstone charm, world-class amenities, and easy access to everything the borough has to offer.

Studio, 1-, and 2-bedroom apartments at 595 Dean feature Caesarstone counters, gas stoves, and modern fixtures throughout. Select apartments include private terraces, extra-high ceilings, and in-unit washer/dryers with alcove layouts available for a home office, nursery, or extra space when you need it.

Above it all, the rooftop pool delivers sweeping Brooklyn views that make this one of the most sought-after addresses in Prospect Heights. Lounge on the sundeck, fire up the BBQ grills on the amenity terrace, or take your workout to the next level with exclusive access to Chelsea Piers Fitness one of Brooklyn's premier fitness destinations, right in your building. The amenity package also includes co-working space with private call booths, a screening room, children's playroom, resident lounge, club room, and concierge pet services through Throw Me A Bone.

Outside, Pacific Park's greenspace, plazas, playground, and dog run are steps away and Prospect Park is right around the corner. The Brooklyn Museum, Brooklyn Botanic Garden, Barclays Center, and Atlantic Terminal are all within easy reach. Explore what makes Prospect Heights one of Brooklyn's most exciting neighborhoods

Our Commitment to Inclusivity

New York City is committed to the principle of inclusivity in all of its neighborhoods, including supporting New Yorkers to reside in neighborhoods of their choice, regardless of their neighborhood of origin and regardless of the neighborhood into which they want to move.

FAQ

General Questions

Through Housing Connect, you can find and apply for affordable rental and homeownership opportunities. To qualify, your household must meet the income and size requirements for a unit in the affordable development. Your household is all of the people who will live in the affordable unit.

Housing is considered affordable if it costs about one-third or less of what the people living there get in income.

The New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) and Housing Development Corporation (HDC) create affordable housing opportunities for many household income levels and sizes. The buildings are privately owned. HPD and HDC have a monitoring and oversight role.

Application Questions

Housing Connect uses two-step verification for creating your account. Your Housing Connect verification code is sent to a different email (or phone number) than your confirmation email. Check the email address or phone number that you entered as your additional contact info when you signed up. If you’re still having trouble, check out the Housing Connect training video titled ‘Account Setup’.

Online: Apply online through Housing Connect when the lottery opens. For detailed instructions, review the Housing Connect Guidebook.

By mail: Paper applications can be requested. The address to request a paper application will be updated once the lottery has officially launched.

After you have created your account, you can view, add, and edit your information from the “My Household” page. After logging in, you’ll see your name with an arrow next to it in the top right-hand corner of the page. Click your name, and a dropdown menu will appear. Click the “My Household” option. This page shows your Household Summary, Household Members, and Housing Choices. Click the light grey “Edit” buttons on the right of each section to add your information. For detailed instructions, see How to Apply.

If you’re still having trouble after reviewing the Applying Online instructions and Housing Connect Training videos, you may want to apply by mail.

It can take several months or longer to hear about your application. Sometimes you might not hear back even if you qualify.

While you’re waiting, carefully check what your current lease says about moving out before the lease is over. If you’re offered an apartment, you might need to move quickly.

If your application is selected, you’ll be invited to respond to a document request. This interview is very important. Agents from the building will confirm if you qualify for the opportunity you applied for. Get ready ahead of time to make sure you’re prepared.

If you aren’t selected or don’t hear back, keep searching for other apartments and apply when you are ready.
